checks.scope: Python exact bounds, fixed-pair and joint tiny-tree census; no product integration, performance, or FULL claim

limitations: Bounds are over continuous boxes; no discrete extremum or production C++ overflow qualification is inferred.
The joint model starts at zero and uses a fixed DFS witness order; its source tree is split at median cardinality, not the midpoint used by the published C++ consumer.
The witness frontier is one cursor in a shared threaded index. Payload links are persistent, but their cumulative allocations and output storage are not a measured resident-memory bound.
The split budget is per product lineage and changes only grain: unresolved pairs continue with the inherited cursor and payload. It does not bound shell storage or total work.
The small judge stores IDs in every node, accumulates output records and expands them for an independent rational oracle. This is not a proposed product memory layout.
Node visits compare two Python model traversals using the same exact bounds and tree order, not the timing or node counts of the other auditor C++ consumer.
Results remain by pair; canonical sphere deduplication, filter integration, WSPD, q3/q4 and HGP FULL are not implemented here.
scope: Independent Python exact bounds and joint q2 continuations over tiny pair products; no production, benchmark or FULL qualification
